name: CyberSec Toolkit
description: Async network security platform with port scanning, live CVE lookup, MITRE ATT&CK mapping, and AI-powered analysis, streamed in real time.
coverAlt: 3D desktop monitor mockup displaying the CyberSec cybersecurity platform website with an AI-powered vulnerability scanning dashboard in a dark purple interface.

designDecisions.title: One workspace, every tool
designDecisions.description: All security tools live in one unified workspace, eliminating constant tab-switching and keeping investigations connected.

designDecisions.title: Context beyond raw results
designDecisions.description: Scan results are enriched with relevant context, helping analysts connect findings and understand potential security risks without manual investigation.

designDecisions.title: Consistency across complexity
designDecisions.description: A shared interface across every tool reduces the learning curve and makes complex security workflows easier to navigate.

designDecisions.title: Reporting without repetition
designDecisions.description: Automated reports turn scan findings into structured, actionable insights, removing the need to manually compile and write reports.

developmentDecisions.title: Pure asyncio scan engine
developmentDecisions.description: The scanner is built on asyncio instead of wrapping nmap. This removes an external dependency, keeps scans streamable, and gives full control over concurrency and output.

developmentDecisions.title: Adaptive speed, bounded impact
developmentDecisions.description: AIMD concurrency and a token-bucket rate limiter tune scan speed to the target. Stealth, normal, and aggressive presets let users trade speed against noise.

developmentDecisions.title: Composable scan pipeline
developmentDecisions.description: Port discovery, banner grabbing, CVE lookup, MITRE ATT&CK mapping, and AI analysis are separate stages, so each one can improve without reshaping the rest.

developmentDecisions.title: Live progress over SSE
developmentDecisions.description: Scans stream results as they happen, and a worker heartbeat with a stale-scan reaper recovers interrupted jobs, so users always know what is running and what is ready to review.

developmentDecisions.title: AI that degrades gracefully
developmentDecisions.description: Analysis runs through Groq, falls back to Gemini, then to rule-based logic. Reports still generate when a provider is down or no key is set.

developmentDecisions.title: Safe by default
developmentDecisions.description: Private IP ranges are blocked, DNS rebinding protection is built in, scan endpoints require JWT, and the API is rate-limited, so the tool is hard to misuse.

name: Designer's Room
description: A roadmap-driven learning and community platform for designers: follow structured guidebooks like UI/UX Designer, learn topic by topic, and share thoughts and experiences with other designers. Think roadmap.sh meets TryHackMe, built for design.
coverAlt: 3D laptop mockup showcasing the Designer's Room platform with a guidebook roadmap page and community feed, in a clean modern interface.

designDecisions.title: One workspace, every tool
designDecisions.description: All security tools live in one place, eliminating tab-switching and keeping the entire investigation workflow connected.

designDecisions.title: Context before complexity
designDecisions.description: Scan results are enriched with relevant context, helping analysts connect findings and understand security risks without manually correlating data.

designDecisions.title: Consistency across tools
designDecisions.description: A unified interface and familiar interaction patterns across every tool reduce the learning curve and make complex investigations easier to navigate.

designDecisions.title: Insights, not manual reports
designDecisions.description: Automated reporting transforms raw scan results into structured, actionable insights, removing repetitive report writing and saving analysts time.

developmentDecisions.title: Content as structured data
developmentDecisions.description: Roadmaps, stages, checkpoints, topics, and progress are separate models. Topic bodies live in their own document table, and progress is keyed per user and topic. A view layer merges them, so the same system can support multiple guidebooks.

developmentDecisions.title: Useful state at every step
developmentDecisions.description: Each topic is done, in-progress, not-started, or locked. The states differ by shape and label, not just color: a check, a dot, an empty ring, and a dimmed ring with a 'Needs: Stage N' pill, plus aria-labels and Review/Start actions.

developmentDecisions.title: Community kept separate from the learning path
developmentDecisions.description: Community is its own area, entered from the roadmap's completion card ('Share your progress'). Learning flow stays focused on topics and progress, and the community layer is built separately instead of cluttering topic pages.

name: Notify-ED
description: Instant multi-channel grade notification platform for colleges: upload a roster, enter marks, and students get Email, WhatsApp and in-app alerts with delivery tracking.
coverAlt: 3D laptop mockup showcasing the Notifyed student grade notification platform website with automated email and WhatsApp alerts, featuring a clean cream and orange interface.

developmentDecisions.title: One mark, many channels
developmentDecisions.description: A single marks submission fans out to email and in-app alerts in parallel, so one channel failing never blocks the others. Providers stay swappable (SMTP or webhook for email, WATI or webhook for WhatsApp), with channel-specific message formatting.

developmentDecisions.title: Validate at the boundary
developmentDecisions.description: Roster upload checks file type and required columns, normalizes cells, and upserts on enrollment number so re-uploads don't duplicate students. Marks are range-checked in the API and enforced again by database constraints before anything is sent.

developmentDecisions.title: Delivery you can audit
developmentDecisions.description: Each email attempt is logged with channel, status, error message and timestamp, linked back to the mark. Failed sends can be retried from the history view, which updates the same log record.

name: Sedative Physio
description: A one-stop learning platform for physiotherapy students: courses, notes and interactive 3D anatomy models in one place, with a free public library and paid courses.
coverAlt: Sedative Physio learning platform homepage showing courses, notes and 3D anatomy resources.

designThinking.problem: Students learn from random PDFs, YouTube and WhatsApp groups, with nothing in one place.
designThinking.coreChallenge: Fit six resource types on one public homepage without scaring a first-timer, and make the paid area feel like a clear next step.
designThinking.research: Competitive analysis of physio and ed-tech platforms, plus case studies of similar problems.
designThinking.process: Collected resources, studied what worked and what didn't, picked a premium palette, and decided what belongs on the homepage versus other pages.

designDecisions.title: Two-part structure
designDecisions.description: A public site for free resources and courses, plus a paid area unlocked after purchase, so the free side earns trust and the paid side feels like a natural next step.

designDecisions.title: A free taste
designDecisions.description: A few complimentary 3D models let people see the value before paying.

designDecisions.title: Homepage restraint
designDecisions.description: Only the essentials live on the homepage. Everything else gets its own page, so a first-timer is never overwhelmed.

designDecisions.title: Trust and hierarchy
designDecisions.description: Clearer hierarchy and trust signals reduce drop-off between landing and checkout.

illustrativeRevenue.assumptions: 5,000 visitors a month, courses priced ₹1,000–5,000, 1–3% conversion.

developmentDecisions.title: The server owns the money
developmentDecisions.description: The client sends only course IDs. Prices are recalculated server-side, payment signatures are verified with a timing-safe HMAC, and order status plus enrollments change in one transaction. Verification and the Razorpay webhook are both idempotent, so a closed tab or a retried webhook can't double-enroll or leave a paid order unfulfilled.

developmentDecisions.title: Clerk owns identity, the app owns domain data
developmentDecisions.description: Credentials and sessions live in Clerk, and the database keeps only the learner profile, orders and enrollments. Profiles sync through signed webhooks, with just-in-time provisioning as a fallback for local sign-ins. Orders are scoped by user ID rather than email, and deleted users are soft-tombstoned so purchase history survives.

developmentDecisions.title: Heavy assets stay off the API
developmentDecisions.description: Note PDFs sit in Cloudflare R2 behind 5-minute presigned URLs, 3D anatomy models are served from jsDelivr, and images are converted to WebP at build time or on demand. API responses are no-store by default, and public routes opt in to CDN caching with ETags.
